analysis:
The change touches documentation only: docs/developer/build.md (toolchain selection text in lines ~162-184 per the patch; the supplied head excerpt, lines 488-708, is unchanged surrounding text) and docs/developer/test.md (a two-line SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 wording update at ~1049). No runtime code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage, fan helper or add-on socket behavior changes, so no changes to TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013 or to T-041 mitigations are visible.

The documented policy is a release toolchain mode (SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 only) versus a qualification mode (27.2 or 27.0). release-provider.yml, provider-signing-validation.yml and master/dispatched release preparation use the stricter release mode. PR/CI use the looser qualification mode, which is not release evidence. This narrows rather than widens the release trust surface. The prose says the toolchain script tries each installed Xcode and exports DEVELOPER_DIR so Metal, xcodebuild and signing use the same Xcode. Whether the script enforces that (e.g., signing and Developer ID steps pinned to the selected Xcode, fallback to a non-accepted SDK) lives in scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and the workflows, which were not supplied. I record that as an unverified integration contract, not a finding.

The docs also state that the Darkbloom Sandbox CI base mirrors the qualification values via images/macos/pins.env. That is a cross-repo dependency (TB-013/T-061 adjacent) not examined here. The supplied head text for build.md shows no new instructions that bypass cache identity checks, state erasure or signing gates; it explicitly retains the human-authorization and exact-build-identity registration statements. No secrets are present. The base text for test.md is consistent with the patch and nothing in it implies a regression.
